name: fx-63eb255a-blind30-ots
instr:
# fx-regen

This is a terminal browser for structured data documents: you hand it a file, it draws the contents as a foldable tree, and from there you move about with the arrow buttons, jump to a numbered row, fold and unfold, take entries out, ask for the result in another shape, and let a shell offer you suggestions as you type. Almost every one of those is now wrong somewhere. The repository has received 22 separate undocumented edits.

Opening a file and letting the very first screen draw is already enough to see it. The dotted address worked out for the selected entry is built as if it never began at the document root, so the addresses handed around no longer agree with the file, and the same flaw shows again the moment the whole document is folded shut with shift and the left arrow. A percentage-style figure drawn alongside the document is worked out against a scale one larger than a hundred, so it reads slightly off at every position. Typing a colon, the number five and Enter to jump to a numbered row goes wrong too: the route worked out for the selection loses its first step, so the entry that ends up selected is not the one at that row. Typing a dotted path such as .foo at the command line to jump straight to an entry by its key fails as well: the path can no longer be made sense of, so no matching entry is found and the jump does nothing.

Taking the document in is unreliable in several ways of its own. Once the reader stumbles over a symbol it cannot make sense of,
